findings.quote: A number about the speaker, such as years of service, supports ethos instead.
findings.problem: Being about the speaker does not make a number an ethos appeal. For example, 'I lost two children in the flood' can appeal to sympathy, making it pathos. Personal income and expense figures can support a logical argument about affordability. Students applying this rule would misclassify appeals. The number's function determines its appeal.
findings.source: [Purdue OWL, Using Rhetorical Strategies for Persuasion](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/general_writing/academic_writing/establishing_arguments/rhetorical_strategies.html), sections Logos, Ethos, and Pathos. Checklist B01.
